title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. X → S is a morphism in characteristic p admitting, locally, a relative p-basis of one element {x}, so it is essentially a smooth relative curve. X^{(p)} is the Frobenius twist, and Λ is a coefficient algebra over Z = (X^{(p)}, Λ). Q is the cokernel of O_{X^{(p)}}⊗Λ → F_*O_X⊗Λ. It is locally free of rank p−1 with basis the classes of x, x², …, x^{p−1}. Via d, Q is identified with the sheaf B of locally exact differentials. Write L = Ω¹_{X^{(p)}/S}⊗Λ.

Previous page. The pairing φ(f,g) = C̃(f dg), with C̃ the Cartier operator, is a perfect Λ-bilinear pairing Q×Q → L. It is alternating for p odd and symmetric for p = 2. Hence Q ≅ Q^∨⊗L, and taking determinants, det Q ≅ (det Q)^{-1}⊗L^{⊗(p−1)}.

This page.
(**) gives a canonical isomorphism det(Q)^{⊗2} ≅ L^{⊗(p−1)}.

Case 1, p = 2. Q has rank 1, and Q^{⊗2} ≅ Ω¹_{X^{(2)}/S}⊗Λ. So the twisted canonical sheaf is canonically a square: Q is a canonical theta characteristic of X^{(2)}, given by the exact differentials. Grothendieck adds two remarks.
- This does not make Ω¹_{X/k} itself a square. Counterexample: a smooth proper rational curve without rational point (a pointless conic). Its ω has degree −2, while its Picard group consists of even degrees only.
- This is consistent: over k in characteristic 2, the conic X^{(2)} has Brauer class 2·[X] = 0, so it has points.
He also asks a question (with a '?') about other 'odd' rank-2 cases.

Case 2, p odd. m = (p−1)/2 is an integer. (**) only determines a square root det Q ≅ L^{⊗m} up to the sign ambiguity μ₂ = Z/2. He wants a canonical ψ: det Q ≅ L^{⊗m}. He tests on the basis ẋ∧ẋ²∧…∧ẋ^{p−1}: under (**) its square goes to Δ·(dx̃)^{⊗(p−1)}, where Δ is the determinant of the matrix of φ. He computes Δ = (−1)^{p−2}·(p−1)!, and with Wilson's theorem (product of the elements of the cyclic group F_p^* is −1) gets Δ = −1.

Next page. He then defines ψ(ẋ∧…∧ẋ^{p−1}) = dx̃^{⊗m}⊗1. He argues independence of the p-basis by a rigidity argument: the scheme of relative p-bases has connected fibres, so a map from it to the trivial double cover (Z/2)_Z is constant.

Purpose. A canonical description of det B and its square root, ultimately towards a global cohomological definition for X proper smooth of relative dimension 1, and a question about higher dimension.
errors: Index slip inherited from the previous page. C̃(x^i dx^j) = j·C̃(x^{i+j−1}dx) is nonzero exactly when i+j−1 ≡ p−1, i.e. i+j = p, not i+j = p−1 as written. With i+j = p−1 the matrix would have only p−2 nonzero entries and be degenerate. The correct matrix has entry p−i = −i in position (i, p−i), which also makes φ visibly alternating.

The sign of the anti-diagonal (p−1)×(p−1) permutation is (−1)^{(p−1)(p−2)/2}, not (−1)^{(p−1)−1}. Hence Δ = (−1)^{(p−1)(p−2)/2}·(p−1)! = (−1)^{(p+1)/2}. So Δ = +1 for p ≡ 3 mod 4 and Δ = −1 for p ≡ 1 mod 4, not −1 always. Check p = 3: matrix [[0,2],[1,0]] has determinant −2 = 1 in F_3.

Consistency check: Δ is the determinant of an alternating matrix, so it must be a square (a Pfaffian squared). The claimed value −1 is not a square in F_p when p ≡ 3 mod 4, which flags the slip. The normalization in (***) on the next page should be adjusted by a sign, or better replaced by the Pfaffian.

The remark about Ω¹_{X/S} being 'lui-même' a square under the hypotheses 'S et X réduit gén., Λ ≅ O' is garbled. As stated it conflicts with the pointless-conic counterexample given just after. What holds canonically is that Ω¹_{X^{(p)}/S}⊗Λ is a square.

ideas.what: Cartier pairing φ(f,g) = C̃(f dg) makes B = F_*O_X/O_{X'} self-dual with values in Ω¹_{X'} (alternating for p odd).
ideas.modern_name: Self-duality B ≅ B^∨⊗ω_{X'} of the sheaf of locally exact differentials
ideas.usually_credited_to: Raynaud, 'Sections des fibrés vectoriels sur une courbe' (1982), and the later literature on Frobenius pushforwards
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as far as I know; this cote contains a 1981 offprint, possibly related to Katz's Cartier-operator / Gauss–Manin material

ideas.what: det(B)^{⊗2} ≅ ω^{⊗(p−1)}, and canonically det(B) ≅ ω^{⊗(p−1)/2} for p odd.
ideas.modern_name: Determinant of B / of F_*O_X (equivalently det F_*O_X ≅ ω^{(1−p)/2} on curves)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Raynaud 1982; later Joshi, Sun Xiaotao and others on Frobenius direct images

ideas.what: For p = 2, B = F_*O_X/O_{X'} is a canonical theta characteristic of X^{(2)}, i.e. B^{⊗2} ≅ ω_{X'}.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical theta characteristic in characteristic 2 (exact differentials / kernel of Cartier)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford (Theta characteristics, 1971) and Raynaud; the attribution of the char-2 remark is unsure

ideas.what: A pointless conic shows Ω¹_{X/k} itself need not be a square, while the Frobenius twist's Ω¹ is.
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (folklore; Atiyah/Mumford theory of theta characteristics)

ideas.what: Removing the μ₂ sign ambiguity of the square root det Q ≅ L^{(p−1)/2} via an explicit formula plus a rigidity/connectedness argument on the scheme of p-bases.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical square root via the Pfaffian of an alternating perfect pairing

ideas.what: Using Wilson's theorem (product of the elements of a cyclic group of even order is −1) to evaluate the discriminant.

missed.claim: Around 1972, in a relative setting (any base S, coefficients Λ, existence of a one-element p-basis rather than smoothness over a field), Grothendieck had three statements. (1) The self-duality of B under the Cartier pairing. (2) det(B)^2 ≅ Ω^{p−1}. (3) For p = 2, B is a canonical square root of Ω¹_{X^{(2)}/S}. These predate Raynaud's 1982 treatment of B, though the results themselves are now standard.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical priority. The relative and Λ-linear formulation is slightly more general than usual textbook statements, but nothing here is likely to be new to specialists.

missed.claim: Two questions are left open: whether the canonical identities (self-duality of B, canonical det B ≅ ω^{(p−1)/2}) extend to higher relative dimension, and a cryptic question about other 'odd rank 2' cases.
missed.quote: ? il y aurait-il des cas impair de rang 2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: In higher dimension the analogous statements concern the complexes B^i, Z^i and the Cartier isomorphism, with det of F_*O_X expressed via K_X. The determinant identities there are known, at least partially, but a canonical square-root/sign refinement is not standard.

deep.surprise_reason: These are early, careful, relative versions of facts later made standard by Raynaud and others: self-duality and determinant of B, and the canonical theta characteristic in characteristic 2. The page has computational slips (the index condition and the sign of Δ), and the Pfaffian, which would remove the sign ambiguity directly, is not used. Interesting for priority, not mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: In the formula for Δ the exponent is written (−1)^{(p−1)−1}; the struck-out right-hand side is '(1.2…(p−1))', not an ellipsis of unknown text.
'Si S {+et X réduit gén. Λ ≃ O_{X^{(p)}}+} et Ω¹_{X/S} est lui-même inversible' should probably read: 'Si S et X réduits, Λ ≃ O_{X^{(p)}}, et Ω¹_{X/S} inversible…'.
'exemple de Serre-Tate-Frohlich' is uncertain; the following illustration is a smooth proper rational curve without rational point (a pointless conic).
'Ref[?] … le … de X^{(p)}' is likely 'Rappelons que si…' or 'Reprenons le cas…'; it is illegible and is followed by 'canonique associé à la situation'.
Last line: 'Comme F_p^* est un groupe cyclique d'ordre pair p−1, le produit de ses éléments est −1, donc on trouve Δ = −1'.
